story_title: Microsoft and NVIDIA Bring Persistent Local AI Agents to Windows PCs
why_this_story: This is a fundamental shift in desktop computing: Microsoft added OS-level containers (MXC) specifically to let AI agents run persistently in the background on Windows, supported by 128GB unified memory laptops from NVIDIA.
viral_angle: Your Windows PC is being rebuilt from the OS level up to host local background AI agents that never hit cloud servers.
story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI agents live in cloud browsers, but Microsoft and NVIDIA just built OS-level primitives and 128GB unified memory hardware to run 125B parameter agents directly on your local laptop.

caption:
Microsoft and NVIDIA just announced a massive architecture shift for Windows PCs: persistent local AI agents.

Instead of sending prompts to cloud servers, Windows is building native OS primitives called Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to govern AI agents executing safely in the background.

To power these background agents, NVIDIA introduced RTX Spark — offering up to 128GB of unified memory on laptops like the Surface Laptop Ultra to run 125B parameter models unmetered and offline.

Is local AI on desktop hardware the future you want, or do you prefer cloud AI?
